subject: HelixPay trial: integration & success criteria (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@helixpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-01-12T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: HelixPay trial: integration & success criteria (post-call recap)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the trial environment: 

Call highlights:
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for transaction enrichment and risk scoring in HelixPay's sandbox flow (500k monthly tokens estimated for the PO C).
- Primary success criteria agreed:
  * Endpoint latency p50 < 120ms at 20rps sustained
  * Accuracy threshold: >= 92% match to current enrichment labels on our standard test set
  * No PII leaves the VPC; logs retained for 30 days per HelixPay policy
- Integration surface: streaming API for real-time enrich; SDK for batch reconciliation; tool-calling prototype for lookup fallback.

My proposed trial timeline:
1) Week 0 (this week): finalise scope + provide SDK route doc and rate-limit spreadsheet (attached).
2) Week 1: HelixPay spins up sandbox credentials + security questionnaire return.
3) Week 2–3: Redwood delivers streaming demo route + SDK example and we run a smoke test.
4) Week 4: Acceptance run and scoring on agreed test set.

Ownership (initial):
- Redwood technical owner: Ben Carter (implementation + sample SDK routes).
- Redwood PM / commercial: me (Jasmine) — mutual action plan and acceptance gate decisions.
- HelixPay technical owner: Tom Becker — sandbox creds and test dataset.

Immediate asks for HelixPay:
- Can you confirm the sandbox CIDR range and preferred auth method (mTLS or API key)?
- Please assign a primary engineer for dev pairing next week.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_routes.md (SDK entry points, example code), mapi_rate_limits.xlsx (expected throughput/limit knobs).

Next steps: if that looks right, Ben will drop the routes file into the Drive folder and we’ll schedule a 60-min pairing session for Wednesday.

Thanks —
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Chen <sarah@helixpay.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>

Date: 2029-01-12T17:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HelixPay trial: integration & success criteria (post-call recap)

Thanks Jasmine — this is very helpful. Confirming a few things from our side: 

1) Auth: we prefer mTLS for the streaming endpoint; API keys are okay for batch SDK calls.
2) Sandbox CIDR: 10.40.0.0/16 (we'll open the range to Redwood infra IPs once we get final IP list).
3) Engineer: assigning Tom as primary (looping him here). He'll also provide the test dataset (anonymised) by Monday EOD.

On success criteria, a couple of clarifications: 
- Latency: p50 < 120ms is fine, but we also want p95 < 350ms for peak bursts.
- Accuracy: we will supply the scoring harness, and we want an initial baseline run within the first acceptance window.

Security question: we need a short summary of where token-level logs live and whether Redwood can redact request/response text before it leaves the VPC. Can Ben provide that in the pairing session?

We can take the Wednesday pairing — prefer 10:00–11:00 PT.

Cheers,
Sarah
Sarah Chen
Head of Integrations, HelixPay
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah@helixpay.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-01-13T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: HelixPay trial: integration & success criteria (post-call recap)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks for the details. Bringing the technical plan into concrete steps below; I'll add the SDK snippets to the Drive before our Wed pairing.

High-level integration plan (technical):
- Streaming route (mTLS): /v1/stream/enrich — bi-directional, contiguous token streaming, supports function/tool-calling for external lookup fallbacks.
  * Defaults: batch_size=1 (real-time), max_seq=512; we can tune for your traffic shape.
  * Rate limits: see attached spreadsheet; default sandbox policy = 25rps bursting to 50rps for 60s.
- Batch SDK route (API key): /v1/sdk/batch-enrich — python/node samples included.
- Tool-calling pattern: a lightweight JSON schema for a lookup call: {"tool":"identity_lookup","query":"..."}; Redwood will proxy calls to HelixPay's lookup endpoint when configured.

Security / logging:
- Logs: token-level traces are written to the customer's VPC logging bucket by default for Private deployments; for Hosted trials we can configure ephemeral logging with automatic redaction.
- Redaction: we support server-side redaction rules (regex-based) applied at ingress — can redact account numbers, emails, and other PII before logs leave the runtime. We'll demonstrate redaction toggles in the pairing session.

Owners & timeline (concrete):
- Jan 13–14: Ben drops code + route docs into Drive; Tom to verify mTLS cert exchange.
- Jan 15: Pairing session (10:00–11:00 PT) — live smoke test: sample streaming request + redaction demo.
- Jan 16–19: Acceptance run and scoring; Redwood runs baseline batch scoring and returns results.

Acceptance deliverables:
- A reproducible notebook for scoring (notebook link will be in Drive).
- Latency and throughput report for the acceptance window.
- A short checklist signed off by Tom confirming dataset and privacy controls.

If that matches what you expect, I'll upload the SDK fragments and a short security one-pager.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
